gates.text: Truth: every quoted snippet and phrase-bank entry is verbatim and traceable to a listed URL; no claim, number, customer or quote that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research.
No fabricated customer evidence: every count (n of N) matches the snippets collected; no composite quotes, personas or inferred demographics.
Pools separated: own-customer, competitor-customer and category-general evidence are never merged into one count or percentage.
Privacy and access: no reviewer names or personal profile data stored; no content obtained behind logins, paywalls or CAPTCHAs.

anchors.1: One source type (e.g. only the business's own testimonials) or sources that don't match where this buyer talks.
anchors.3: Two or three source types, roughly fitting the business type, but competitor reviews or forums thin.
anchors.5: Three or more source types matched to the business type: own reviews, top competitors' critical reviews and 2+ forum threads; inaccessible sources listed.

anchors.1: No coding, or themes asserted without tagging snippets.
anchors.3: Snippets tagged with themes but four forces applied loosely; generic praise counted as evidence.
anchors.5: Every snippet coded for force, job, alternative, trigger, objection and segment clues where stated; generic praise excluded from themes.

anchors.3: Counts given for some themes, denominators or source spread missing.
anchors.5: Every theme ranked with n of N, number of distinct sources and intensity; findings vs signals labelled by the 3-snippets/2-sources rule.

anchors.1: Paraphrased or business-voice phrases; no sources.
anchors.3: Verbatim phrases with sources but ungrouped or mostly unusable in copy.
anchors.5: 20–40 verbatim phrases grouped by problem, category, trigger, outcome, objection and proof; high-confidence language marked; words to use/avoid list.

anchors.3: Objections in customer words with frequency, but counters generic or missing.
anchors.5: Objections in customer words with force, frequency and source; each counter typed (risk reversal, proof, migration help, anchor) and marked existing vs 'owner to decide'.

anchors.3: Specific observations but no tension or implication.
anchors.5: 3–7 insights, each a want-versus-fear tension with counts and a concrete implication for positioning, offer or copy.

anchors.1: Presents thin or skewed evidence as conclusive.
anchors.3: Mentions sample size but not date range, skew or authenticity.
anchors.5: States N per pool, date range, inaccessible sources, platform skew and review-authenticity flags; confidence label per insight.

anchors.1: A data dump with no direction.
anchors.3: Some suggestions for copy or positioning.
anchors.5: Hand-off gives headline candidates in customer words, theme-rooted ad angles, top objections for FAQs and the open questions only the owner can answer.
